page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The virtual machine provides 16 dedicated physical cores running AWS Neoverse-V2 processors at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz, with 1 thread per core. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. For high-speed temporary caching and high-throughput data access, the configuration bundles a 950 GB local NVMe SSD instance store, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional memory throughput and strong multi-core scaling. The instance achieved a top-tier result in the PassMark memory benchmark (3295.63), reinforced by top-quartile performance in uncached large-block read (296.82 GB/sec) and write (133.57 GB/sec) bandwidth tests. Multi-core compute capabilities are robust, showing strong performance in the Geekbench multi-core suite (15912.0) and PassMark database operations (24154.6). While single-core calculations and general compression tasks align with average benchmarks, complex workloads like larger LLM prompt processing show lower throughput due to the absence of dedicated GPU acceleration.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the m8gd.4xlarge stems from its dedicated ARM core topology and included low-latency NVMe scratch storage, which eliminates the need to attach separate provisioned block volumes for temporary data. It is well-matched for mid-sized relational and NoSQL databases, transactional analytics, in-memory caching systems, CI/CD artifact building, and general-purpose backend web services.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.4xlarge is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine utilizing 16 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.8 GHz, supported by 64.0 GB of memory and an integrated 950 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with an 8 Gbps baseline network, the instance yields top-tier memory scores and strong multi-core throughput, highlighted by high uncached memory bandwidth and strong database transaction results. Single-threaded metrics and general compute sit within standard mid-range distributions, while heavy tensor computations are limited by the absence of discrete GPU hardware. The combination of dedicated physical cores and integrated high-speed local NVMe storage delivers strong resource efficiency without requiring extra provisioned block storage for scratch workloads, making it a reliable fit for relational databases, Redis caching layers, microservices, and containerized backend platforms.
